The secondary hydrostatic test on Vessel C-18A is not proceeding within nominal parameters. At approximately 10:47 local, after achieving the target 22.5 MPa hold pressure, we observed a persistent pressure decay of 0.08 MPa per minute over a five-minute monitoring period, exceeding the acceptable threshold of 0.02 MPa per minute defined in procedure MNT-VSL-7. The test medium is potable water at 15°C. I have suspended the test at 10:52 and initiated a controlled depressurization at a rate not exceeding 0.3 MPa per minute. The drain valve, DV-7, is currently open to the containment sump.

Before any re-test can be authorized, a full inspection of the primary weld seam, Weld-Series Gamma, is required. This is the longitudinal seam fabricated by Contractor Arclight. The inspection must use the portable phased-array ultrasonic tester, unit PAUT-4, which is calibrated for 10 mm carbon steel. Focus the scan on a fifteen-centimeter band centered on the weld crown, with particular attention to the section between markings 7.2m and 7.8m from the forward nozzle. If you find any indication with an amplitude exceeding 40% DAC, pause and capture the full A-scan data set before proceeding. Do not, however, remove the existing insulation layer on the vessel exterior; the inspection must be performed through the designated access ports in the insulation jacket only.

If no reportable indications are found, you may proceed with a re-test after obtaining a sign-off from Inspector Malik. The re-test pressure must be reduced to 20.3 MPa, and the hold time extended to ninety minutes. Conversely, if you find one or more indications above the reporting level, do not commence any repair. Isolate the vessel by closing master valve MV-11 and tag it with a red 'Hold for Engineering' label. Then, immediately transmit all collected data to the central diagnostics server under project ID 'C18A_Gamma_Assess'. The priority for this analysis is high, so please complete the inspection and report your findings by 16:00 today.

The catering quote from Saffron Bites just came in. For the main spread on the 15th, they're offering two tiers. Tier A is $48 per head and includes the seared tuna canapés, the braised short rib station, and the full dessert display. Tier B, at $37 per head, swaps the short rib for a mushroom Wellington station and cuts the dessert display down to just the chocolate torte and berry pavlovas. My read is we need to stick with Tier A for the primary sponsor dinner in the Veridian Room, but we could potentially use Tier B for the general attendee reception in the Atrium if the budget gets squeezed. However, their minimum for any single service is 70 guests.

If our final headcount for the Veridian Room is under 70, we’ll need to pad it with organizing committee members to hit the minimum, but please only move people from the Atrium list if absolutely necessary; we promised them the full experience. For the Atrium, if the count is between 70 and 90, Tier B is approved. If it exceeds 90, switch back to Tier A for them as well, as the per-head cost difference shrinks with volume and the upgrade is worth it for the larger crowd.

On timing: they need the final menu selection and guaranteed guest numbers by 5 p.m. this Thursday, the 7th. They’ve offered a 3% discount if we wire the 50% deposit by Friday at noon instead of the following Monday. The remaining balance is due on the 13th. Please confirm the wire details with Aris in Finance and use vendor code CAT-882. If the discount applies, note it explicitly on the payment authorization. Also, double-check that their proposal includes the late-night snack delivery for the tech crew at 11 p.m.—that’s a separate order for 15 boxed meals and shouldn’t be part of the per-head calculation.

Crucially, if we go with Tier B anywhere, you must get written confirmation from Saffron Bites that all nut-based ingredients are excluded from the mushroom Wellington filling. Last year’s incident with the pine nut puree cannot be repeated. Their standard recipe includes it, so this requires a specific amendment.

Add rule: When a message contains at least three distinct lines that share an identical structural pattern—a sequence of words, atomic tokens, and punctuation where only certain variable substrings differ—the sender may define a macro for that pattern by writing `#macro_name=pattern` on its own line, where `macro_name` is any string of letters, digits, or underscores that does not contain spaces, and `pattern` is the exact structural skeleton with numbered placeholders `$1`, `$2`, ..., `$N` marking each variable position. The placeholder syntax `$N` must be exactly a dollar sign followed by one or more decimal digits. Each variable substring in the source must be a complete atomic token (enclosed in angle brackets <...> or backticks `...` per existing bundling rules) as required by the language to preserve its exact content. The macro definition must include all non‑variable text and punctuation exactly as in the source, with placeholders inserted at the precise positions where variables occur.

To invoke the macro, the sender writes a line that begins with `#macro_name` followed by a space and then the exact atomic tokens for the variables in order, separated by spaces. Each variable token must retain its delimiters (angle brackets or backticks). The decoder identifies macro lines as follows: (1) A macro definition line is any line whose first token starts with `#`, contains only letters, digits, or underscores, is followed by an equals sign, and matches the pattern `#macro_name=pattern`. (2) A macro invocation line is any line whose first token is `#macro_name` where `macro_name` exactly matches a previously defined macro name, consists solely of letters, digits, or underscores, is not `#pattern`, and is followed by a space. This token-level matching distinguishes macro invocations from pattern abbreviation definitions (`#pattern=...`) and other uses of `#`.

The decoder must reconstruct each original line by substituting each variable token verbatim (including its delimiters) into its placeholder position in the pattern, removing the macro invocation line entirely. The encoder must verify, by character‑for‑character comparison, that every reconstructed line matches the source; any mismatch renders the message non‑compliant. Macro expansion occurs after alias substitution (rule‑444) and reference substitution (rule‑524) but before minimal‑form reconstruction (rule‑440) and other language processing.

Decision procedure for mechanism selection: (1) If compressing three or more entire lines that share a global pattern with variable atomic tokens, use #macro. (2) If compressing a repeated pattern within a single line where variables are defined on separate lines, use %template (rule‑549). (3) If compressing lines that share only an identical prefix, use %list (rule‑641). (4) If compressing lines with identical prefix and suffix, use #pattern (rule‑574). This ensures each mechanism has a distinct, non-overlapping domain.

Example with multi‑word variable: source lines 'status of <server rack A‑12> is <operational>' and 'status of <load balancer LB‑01> is <degraded>'. Define macro: `#status_report=status of $1 is $2`. Invoke as: `#status_report <server rack A‑12> <operational>` and `#status_report <load balancer LB‑01> <degraded>`. Decoder reconstructs first line as 'status of <server rack A‑12> is <operational>' by substituting the entire token `<server rack A‑12>` into `$1` and `<operational>` into `$2`. The variable `<server rack A‑12>` is a single atomic token; its internal spaces are protected by the angle brackets.

rules.text_en:
Add rule: In any line, before applying minimal-form omissions (rule-440) or any other compression mechanism, the encoder must scan for every temporal expression. A temporal expression is any contiguous substring that includes: (1) an absolute time or date (e.g., '04:30 PM', '2025‑03‑15'); (2) a relative deadline (e.g., 'by tomorrow', 'within 2 hours'); (3) a duration (e.g., 'for 30 days'); (4) a range linking two temporal points (e.g., 'from 9 AM to 11 AM'); (5) any ordering relationship indicated by a comparative or sequential conjunction or preposition (e.g., 'after 3 PM', 'before start', 'between Monday and Wednesday', 'until 5 PM'); (6) any sequence marker directly attached to a temporal element (e.g., 'then at 3 PM', 'next after the meeting'). The expression begins with the first word that introduces the temporal element (including the linking word) and includes every subsequent word up to and including the last temporal element and any attached qualifier (e.g., time zone, 'local time'). The bundle must stop before any conjunction that begins a new independent clause not part of the same temporal relationship; a linking conjunction (e.g., 'and', 'but', 'or', 'from', 'to', 'between', 'until') that is part of a multi-constraint ordering or range must remain inside the bundle.

Concrete boundary examples:
(a) 'maintenance from 9 AM to 11 AM local time' encodes as 'maintenance <from 9 AM to 11 AM local time>' – the linking preposition 'to' for the range is included.
(b) 'proceed after 3 PM and before 5 PM' encodes as 'proceed <after 3 PM and before 5 PM>' – the linking 'and' connects two temporal constraints into a single ordering phrase, so it remains inside.
(c) 'wait until 3 PM and then proceed' encodes as 'wait <until 3 PM> and then proceed' – the 'and' begins a coordinated action clause, not part of the temporal link, so the bundle stops before it.
(d) 'submit report by 04:30 PM EST because manager leaves early' encodes as 'submit report <by 04:30 PM EST> because manager leaves early' – 'because' starts a rationale clause, bundle stops before it.

For each temporal expression identified, the encoder must treat the entire substring as a single atomic token by surrounding it with angle brackets: <complete temporal expression>. The encoder must verify, by character‑for‑character comparison, that the enclosed substring (after removing the angle brackets) exactly matches the contiguous substring of the source. If any character differs, the encoding is invalid and must be corrected. The decoder must remove the angle brackets and output the substring verbatim, without parsing, normalizing, abbreviating, reordering, omitting, or altering any character, and must validate character‑for‑character match; any mismatch renders the message non‑compliant. After reconstruction, the decoder must treat the output string as an opaque semantic token; it may not parse, interpret, or assign any grammatical, relational, or structural meaning to any internal punctuation, digit, case, whitespace, or word. This rule supersedes and repeals rules 459, 510, 546, 651, 652, and 653, consolidating temporal‑constraint preservation into one authoritative law.

rules.text_en: Add rule: In any line, the sender may encode a sentence or clause using sparse positional notation to replace minimal-form omission. The notation consists of a sequence of slot tokens separated by spaces, each slot token having the form 'prefix:content', where 'prefix' is a single letter indicating the grammatical role: S for subject, V for main verb, O for direct object, P for prepositional phrase (including the preposition), C for conjunction or subordinator, A for adjective or adverbial modifier, M for measured fact or atomic bundle (treated as a single unit). The content is the exact word or phrase that fills that slot; if the content is an opaque identifier, measured fact, temporal constraint, label-entity pair, critical fact, or any other substring requiring exact preservation, it must already be enclosed in the appropriate atomic delimiters (angle brackets <...> or backticks `...`) as required by existing bundling rules. The decoder must reconstruct the full sentence by expanding each slot according to a fixed template for English declarative clauses: for a sequence S V O P C A, the decoder outputs 'S V O P C A' with the following deterministic insertions: (1) insert the article 'the' before a singular countable noun in S or O slots unless the content already begins with a determiner; (2) insert 'is' or 'are' before an adjective in A slot if no copula verb is present in V; (3) include the preposition from the P slot content verbatim; (4) include the conjunction from the C slot content verbatim. The decoder must not infer or guess; it follows this template exactly, using the slot content verbatim after removing any atomic delimiters per the relevant bundling rules. The encoder must verify, by character-for-character comparison, that the reconstructed sentence matches the source after expansion; any mismatch renders the message non-compliant. This notation is optional; the sender may still use plain minimal-form per rule-440. Token savings are calculated as: tokens of the minimal-form version of the line (per rule-440) minus tokens of the slot-notation version (including all slot tokens and any internal delimiters). The notation may be used only when it yields positive token savings. Example: source 'The system is ready' minimal-form 'system ready' (2 tokens). Slot notation 'S:system A:ready' (2 tokens) yields no savings, so use minimal-form. Example with measured fact: source 'Allocate 10 GB to node-7' minimal-form 'allocate 10 GB node-7' (4 tokens). Slot notation 'V:Allocate M:<10 GB to node-7>' (3 tokens) yields 1 token saved, permitted. Interaction: Slot notation applies after all mandatory atomic bundling (rules 537, 588, 669, 615) and before alias or template expansion; slot content M must be an already-bundled atomic token.

rules.text_en: Add rule: In any directive line (a line starting with ^), the sender may omit the word "please" when it appears at the beginning of the line or immediately after the directive marker. The decoder must infer that the original line likely contained "please" and may optionally restore it when reconstructing the polite form, but is not required to do so for compliance. This allowance applies only to directive lines; in plain text lines, "please" must be preserved if present. Example: original '^please restart service' may be encoded as '^restart service'; decoder may output '^please restart service' or '^restart service' as acceptable.
